Alaska.Ai — Anchorage Desk Draft

2026-06-18 · branch claude/linkedin-desk-2026-06-18
No defensible target this cycle. Four scout slices ran (founders, operators, municipal, research) for the May 19 – June 18, 2026 window. Five candidates were surfaced; all failed the seven-point anti-puff gate. Two were presented to the validator; both failed multiple gates. No broadening was applied (only available candidate outside the 30-day window falls 94 days out — far beyond the 45-day retry threshold). The gate was not lowered. This is a correct outcome.

Validator's Note

Both candidates presented to the validator fail multiple gates at the 30-day window. Broadening to 45 days (to May 4, 2026) was considered but yields no additional candidates: the scouts' only other surfaced candidate (Troy Goldie/GCI/Databricks, March 16, 2026) falls 94 days before the run date, well outside even the 45-day broadened window. The 45-day broadening was therefore not executed. Candidate 1 (Wilber/Tyler): Fails Gate 1 — MOA Finance Department page names Philippe D. Brice as CFO, not Wilber; no independently fetchable institutional source resolves this. Fails Gate 3 — no AI component in the Anchorage contract. Fails Gate 4 — all three corroborators are downstream reprints of one BusinessWire press release. Candidate 2 (Hiratsuka/symposium paper): Fails Gate 2 — primary source paywalled (HTTP 403); decision content unconfirmable. Fails Gate 3 — symposium perspectives paper is not a binary operational decision. Fails Gate 4 — cited corroborator is a different 2025 paper, not the 2026 Hiratsuka paper. This is an honest no-target cycle. The Anchorage AI primary-source pool is thin for the May 19 to June 18 window; both candidates surface real actors and real events but neither meets the bar for consequential, independently corroborated, AI-specific binary decisions owned by a named Anchorage-bowl subject.

Dropped Candidates (5 total)

Lance Wilber — Alleged Chief Fiscal Officer, Municipality of Anchorage

2026-05-26 · 30-day
Gate failed: named_subject, decision_consequential, multi_source_corroboration

Decision: Selected Tyler Technologies enterprise Payments platform for MOA, May 26, 2026

Reason: Gate 1 (Named Subject): The MOA's own institutional Finance Department page names Philippe D. Brice as the current Chief Fiscal Officer, not Lance Wilber. No independently fetchable institutional source — no MOA leadership page, no mayoral press release, no MOA staff directory — confirms Wilber holds the CFO role. The only sources naming Wilber as CFO are the Tyler Technologies BusinessWire press release and its downstream reprints (GovTech, Must Read Alaska, StockTitan). Gate 1 fails. Gate 3 (Decision Consequential): The Anchorage contract is for Tyler's enterprise Payments platform — a cloud-based billing and collections system. No AI component is named in the Anchorage contract. AI is referenced only in relation to Tyler's general corporate roadmap, not the Anchorage deal itself. Inferential chain (Tyler pursues AI products, therefore this contract eventually touches AI) is explicitly prohibited as equivalent to the GCI/Quintillion fiber-enables-AI pattern. Gate 3 fails. Gate 4 (Multi-Source Corroboration): Must Read Alaska is an explicit BusinessWire press release reprint. StockTitan is a press release aggregation service. GovTech draws from the same BusinessWire announcement. All three named corroborators are downstream of the single Tyler Technologies press release — one source amplified, not independent corroboration. Gate 4 fails.

Vanessa Hiratsuka — Senior Researcher, Southcentral Foundation; affiliate faculty, UAA Center for Human Development

2026-05-23 · 30-day
Gate failed: recent_decision, decision_consequential, multi_source_corroboration

Decision: Co-authored 'Artificial intelligence/machine learning in Alaska Native healthcare systems: symposium perspectives,' International Journal of Circumpolar Health, published May 23, 2026

Reason: Gate 2 (Recent Decision): Primary source (Tandfonline DOI 10.1080/22423982.2026.2677426) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Paper title and Epub date confirmed via PubMed (PMID 42176020), but decision content and Hiratsuka's specific authorship cannot be confirmed from a live fetchable page. Gate 2 conditionally fails on unconfirmable primary-source content. Gate 3 (Decision Consequential): A journal publication documenting symposium perspectives does not constitute a binary decision (approve/block, fund/cut, launch/halt). The paper records what 31 symposium participants discussed in 2025; it does not commit a named actor to a specific operational action with a concrete enforcement mechanism confirmable from a fetchable page. Gate 3 fails. Gate 4 (Multi-Source Corroboration): The cited corroborator (PMC12009764) is confirmed by fetch to be a different 2025 paper (Brian Travis Rice et al., 'Community-engaged artificial intelligence') — not the Hiratsuka 2026 symposium paper. The 2025 paper confirms the consortium but does not corroborate the specific 2026 paper or Hiratsuka's decision ownership in it. No second independently fetchable source for the specific 2026 paper was located. Gate 4 fails.

Rohit Mahajan — Co-Founder and CEO, MyEyesAI

Q2 2026 (unconfirmed in window) · dropped at orchestrator level before validation
Gate failed: recent_decision

Decision: Q2 2026 multi-clinic pilot launch in Anchorage-area ophthalmology clinics

Reason: Primary sources (gener8tor press release March 13, Alaska Business Magazine March 11) predate the May 19 window. The Q2 clinic pilot start is described as planned/future; no primary or corroborating source confirms the specific activation date falls within the May 19 to June 18 window.

Erik Williams — Co-Founder and CEO, beadedcloud

2026-06-10 · dropped at orchestrator level before validation
Gate failed: decision_consequential

Decision: Presented pipeline fatigue-prediction capability at ICGSM 2026, June 10, 2026

Reason: A conference presentation does not constitute a business decision binary (funding close, product launch, customer sign, exec hire, pivot, shutdown). No dollar/contract consequence attached to the ICGSM presentation.

Troy Goldie — Senior Vice President and CTO, GCI Communication Corp.

2026-03-16 · dropped at orchestrator level before validation
Gate failed: recent_decision

Decision: Selected Databricks as enterprise AI and data platform; case study published March 16, 2026

Reason: March 16, 2026 is 94 days before the run date — outside even the 45-day broadened window (which opens to May 4, 2026).

Editor's Note

Run summary: All four scout slices completed within the 8-minute timeout window. No transient API errors required retries. Window broadening to 45 days was evaluated but not applied because the only additional candidate (Troy Goldie/GCI/Databricks, March 16, 2026) falls 94 days before the run date, outside even the 45-day threshold.

Notable near-misses:

  • Lance Wilber / MOA / Tyler Technologies (May 26, 2026): In-window, well-documented. Failed on three grounds: (1) MOA institutional page names a different CFO; (2) Anchorage contract has no AI component; (3) all three cited corroborators trace back to the same BusinessWire press release.
  • Vanessa Hiratsuka / Southcentral Foundation (May 23, 2026): Genuine AI-governance paper with real consequence for 150,000+ Alaska Native healthcare beneficiaries. Failed because primary source is paywalled (HTTP 403), the paper is a symposium perspectives publication not an operational binary, and the cited corroborator is a different 2025 paper.
  • Troy Goldie / GCI / Databricks (March 16, 2026): Strongest operator candidate; GCI's first-ever CTO selects enterprise AI platform for Alaska's largest telecom. Outside window by 94 days. Watch for any GCI AI announcement in a future window.

Watch list for next cycle (June 19 – July 18, 2026):

  • STAK Energy DNR final lease decision (comment period closed June 15 — DNR final determination expected; Sparrow Mahoney is off-limits through issue 12, but the DNR Commissioner or decision-maker could be a new subject)
  • GCI AI announcements (Troy Goldie, any in-window decision)
  • Alaska AI data center development at military bases (DAF RFLP issued June 5 for three Alaska bases — watch for named Anchorage-bowl decision-makers in responses or awards)
  • Vanessa Hiratsuka / SCF AI governance paper — if independent non-paywalled coverage emerges, this could qualify with a new citing article
  • MyEyesAI (Rohit Mahajan) — if a clinic-start announcement appears from an independent source with a specific date in window

No deviations from protocol: Four parallel scouts launched as specified, validator received merged candidates, no subagent stalls occurred, no window broadening applied, no image rendered (no-target cycle).
